My research develops data-driven methods to make transportation systems safer, more efficient, and more equitable. Below are the main themes my lab works on; see [Projects](projects.qmd) for active and past funded work, and [Publications](publications.qmd) for the resulting papers.
::: {.plain-grid}
Modeling and controlling traffic dynamics on freeways and arterials, including signal timing, ramp metering, and macroscopic/microscopic simulation of mixed human-driven and automated traffic.
### Transportation Safety Analytics Statistical and machine-learning methods for crash prediction, near-miss detection, and proactive safety management using naturalistic driving and infrastructure sensor data.
### Connected & Automated Vehicles Evaluating how connected-vehicle (CV) and automated-vehicle (AV) technologies affect network performance, safety, and energy use, with a focus on transition-period challenges.
### Transit Equity & Accessibility Measuring and improving access to public transit for underserved populations, combining GTFS data, land-use models, and accessibility metrics to inform service planning.
### Freight & Urban Logistics Understanding last-mile delivery, curb management, and freight network resilience in growing urban areas.
### Applied Machine Learning for Mobility Data Developing interpretable ML methods for large-scale mobility datasets, including probe-vehicle data, video-derived trajectories, and mobile-phone location data.
:::
::: {.split} ::: {} ### Methods & Tools My group works with a mix of field data collection, high-fidelity traffic simulation (e.g., SUMO, VISSIM), statistical modeling, and machine learning. We prioritize reproducible, open-source workflows — code for select projects is available on [GitHub](https://github.com). ::: ::: {} ### Collaborations I collaborate with researchers in computer science, urban planning, and public health, as well as with public-sector partners including [State DOT], [Regional Transit Agency], and [City Department of Transportation]. [Get in touch](contact.qmd) about collaborating. ::: :::
